h1: The 7 Best Aprilaire Whole-House Humidifiers for Dry Winters, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 Aprilaire whole-house humidifiers compared on gallons per day, steam vs evaporative, sensors, coverage and price tier.
summary: The AprilAire 720MKZ is the best value, with 21 gallons per day at the $200 to $500 tier. The 800 steam model is the choice for large airtight homes, up to 10,300 square feet, and the 720AKZ has the easiest water-panel swap. The 500M and 600M suit smaller houses.
intro: Choosing a whole-house humidifier by model number alone is how people end up with a unit too weak for their house. Aprilaire's range runs from the entry 500M to the top-end 800 steam model, and the real divider is how the water gets turned into moisture: bypass airflow, a powered fan, or steam. The model number tells you little about which one you are buying.

We ranked seven Aprilaire models by output, design type, sensors and price, using listings and maker specs. Our listing data names 21 gallons per day for the 720 pair, 12 for the 500M and 10,300 square feet for the 800, and says nothing about other ratings, so we flag the gaps rather than fill them with guesses. Size to your house, not to a number on a box.

products.name: AprilAire 720MKZ Fan-Powered Humidifier, 21 GPD
products.verdict: 21 gallons per day, a hybrid fan and a manual control, without stepping up to the top price tier.
products.description:
The 720MKZ is a whole-house fan-powered evaporative humidifier rated at 21 gallons per day. A hybrid fan evens out airflow, the included manual control mounts on a duct or wall, and the fan module can be reconfigured to fit tight furnace installs. Retail falls between $200 and $500.

It wins because it delivers the same 21 GPD as the pricier 720AKZ for far less. Fan-powered units pull air through the humidifier on their own instead of depending on furnace pressure, which is why they cope with larger and drier homes than bypass models like the 500M and 600M.

Buy it for a big house with a forced-air furnace and a competent installer. The manual control means you adjust humidity yourself with the season, unlike the dual-sensor models.
products.idealFor: Large forced-air homes that want high output without the top price.

products.name: AprilAire 800 Whole-House Steam Humidifier
products.verdict: Electrode steam for up to 10,300 square feet, with dual sensors.
products.description:
The 800 is a steam humidifier built on electrode technology and made in the USA. It is rated for tightly built houses of up to 10,300 square feet and uses dual sensors to respond to both indoor and outdoor conditions. Expect to spend $500 or more.

It ranks second because steam does not rely on furnace airflow, so it works with any heating system and can humidify when the furnace is not running. The tradeoff is cost: the unit is the priciest here, it draws electricity to make steam and it needs a drain, which adds installation work.

Buy it for a large, airtight home or a house with heat pumps or radiant heat. Skip it if you have a standard furnace and a smaller house, where a fan-powered model does the same job for less.

products.name: AprilAire 720AKZ Fan-Powered Evaporative Humidifier, 21 GPD
products.verdict: 21 GPD with a pop-in disposable water panel, but at the $500+ tier.
products.description:
The 720AKZ delivers 21 gallons per day and is built with sustainability in mind. It uses a one-piece disposable hydrocore water panel cartridge that pops in. Expect to spend $500 or more.

It ranks third because it matches the 720MKZ on output but costs more. The reason to pay is the water panel: a one-piece panel that pops in makes the yearly swap a short job, rather than a fiddly one.

Buy it if you will do maintenance yourself and want the easiest panel change. Otherwise the 720MKZ is the sensible buy, since the output is the same and the price is lower.
products.idealFor: Owners who want the simplest annual panel replacement.

products.name: AprilAire 700 Whole-House Humidifier
products.verdict: Fan-powered with dual sensors that respond to outdoor conditions, at the upper price tier.
products.description:
The 700 draws warm furnace air across its evaporator pad, uses dual sensors to track indoor and outdoor conditions, and is made in the USA. Expect to spend $500 or more.

It ranks fourth because the dual sensor setup automates what the 700M and 720MKZ make you do by hand: as the weather turns colder it adjusts the target humidity to avoid window condensation. It lacks the output figure our top picks list, though.

Buy it if you want set-and-forget humidity in a house with a furnace. Check the output rating with an installer, since the listing here gives no gallons-per-day number.
products.idealFor: Homeowners who want automatic humidity control.
products.skipIf: You prefer to set humidity by hand.

products.name: AprilAire 700M Whole-House Fan-Powered Humidifier
products.verdict: The fan-powered design at the $200 to $500 tier, with a single sensor.
products.description:
The 700M is a fan-powered humidifier that pulls heated air directly from the furnace and uses one sensor built into the standard control to monitor indoor conditions. It is made in the USA and retails between $200 and $500.

It ranks fifth since it uses a single indoor sensor, where the 700 uses two. That means it does not adjust for outdoor temperature, so you may see window fog on cold nights unless you lower the setpoint.

Buy it for a mid-size house with a furnace and a limited budget. It does not list an output figure here, so confirm sizing with the installer.
products.idealFor: Mid-size furnace homes on a mid-range budget.

products.name: AprilAire 600M Whole-House Humidifier
products.verdict: A bypass model that protects furnishings from dry air, at the $200 to $500 tier.
products.description:
The 600M is a whole-house humidifier with a single indoor sensor in the standard control, made in the USA, and designed to protect items in the home that are sensitive to dry air. Retail falls between $200 and $500.

It ranks sixth because it is a bypass-style unit and the fan-powered 700M and 720MKZ outpace it on airflow. The tradeoff is simplicity: bypass models have fewer moving parts and fit more furnace layouts.

Buy it for a moderate house where wood floors and instruments need protection from winter dryness. A bypass unit will not keep up in a very large home, so choose a fan-powered or steam model there.
products.idealFor: Moderate homes with wood floors or instruments.
products.skipIf: You have a very large house.

products.name: AprilAire 500M Whole-House Humidifier
products.verdict: The simplest AprilAire whole-house unit, at the $200 to $500 tier.
products.description:
The 500M is the entry whole-house unit, made in the USA, with a single indoor sensor in its standard control and designed to preserve items vulnerable to dry conditions. Retail falls between $200 and $500.

It ranks last because it has the lowest capacity, around 12 gallons per day on the 12-gallon listing, against 21 on the 720 models. It is also a bypass design that depends on furnace airflow.

Buy it for a small to mid-size house with a furnace. Skip it for a large home, because it will run constantly and still struggle in deep winter.
products.skipIf: You live in a large, dry house.

whatMatters.detail: Gallons per day is the water the unit can add to the air over 24 hours, and it is the closest thing to a power rating. The 720 models list 21 GPD and the 500M about 12. A leaky, large or older home needs more than a tight small one. Match the rating to square footage, ask an installer to size it, and check the figure is actually listed.

The design type is how the unit turns water into vapor. Bypass units use furnace pressure and are simple but weak. Fan-powered units like the 700 and 720 pull heated air through the pad and suit bigger homes. Steam, like the 800, uses electrodes and works without furnace airflow, at a cost in power. Read the type in the title before comparing output.

The control type decides who watches the humidity. A manual control has you adjust it as the weather changes, which most people forget. Dual-sensor models like the 700 and 800 track indoor and outdoor conditions, preventing window condensation on cold nights. Look for the words dual sensor or automatic in the listing, and the setpoint range if given.

Evaporative units pass air through a water panel that catches minerals and needs replacing, typically once a year. Skip the swap and scale builds, airflow drops and output falls. The 720AKZ's one-piece pop-in panel is the easiest. Look in the listing for the panel type and its replacement interval, then count the yearly cost as part of ownership.

A whole-house humidifier connects to the furnace plenum, a water line and often a drain, and steam units add an electrical supply. That is plumbing and ductwork, not a plug-in appliance. Budget for a pro installer and confirm the unit fits your furnace layout. Ask whether it needs a drain, because that decides where the unit can go.

faq.q: Will it work with my furnace?
faq.a: Bypass and fan-powered models like the 600M and 700M need a forced-air furnace to carry moisture through the ducts. The 800 steam works without furnace airflow, so it can suit a house with unusual HVAC. Always confirm fit with an installer before buying.

Setting humidity too high in winter. Window condensation means the setpoint is too high for the outdoor temperature, which can damage frames and trim. The dual-sensor 700 and 800 adjust automatically, while manual units like the 720MKZ ask you to lower it as it gets colder.

faq.q: Is steam worth it over evaporative?
faq.a: Only for large or airtight homes. The AprilAire 800 is listed up to 10,300 square feet but costs more to buy and run than the 720MKZ, so evaporative is the better value when 21 GPD is enough for your house.

Whole-house units connect to the furnace, a water line and sometimes a drain. A fan-powered unit like the 720MKZ can be reconfigured for tight installs where space around the plenum is limited. A pro will set the mount and check the water line.

Replace the water panel yearly and clean the unit at the start of each season. The 720AKZ's one-piece pop-in panel is the quickest swap, which makes it easier to actually do. Ignoring the panel is the most common reason output falls.

faq.q: Can it fix dry skin and static?
faq.a: It raises indoor humidity, which usually reduces static shocks and dry skin in winter. It is not a medical treatment, and a hygrometer helps you keep levels comfortable. Too much moisture causes condensation, so aim for a middle range.

finalTake: The 720MKZ is the AprilAire to buy for most large homes, and the 800 steam is for airtight or very large houses. Choose the 700 for automatic sensing and the 500M or 600M for smaller homes. Size the unit with an installer, and replace the water panel every year.
